question: Is a supported Windows app-control release operation plus explicit release verification currently exposed?
conclusion: No such operation or verification status is documented or exposed in the examined installed and available tool surface. Do not acquire a new GUI-control session under the current user gate.
current_desktop_control_state: unverified; not observed by this review
scope_qualification: This is a bounded finding for currently installed documentation and exposed tools. It does not establish global impossibility, undocumented implementation behavior, or the state of another version.

api_findings.window_state_qualification: These describe a selected app window and do not expose ownership/release confirmation.
api_findings.guidance_interruption_rule: Stop issuing app input when the tool reports an ended turn or user stop.
api_findings.guidance_reset_rule: Reset is described as helper recovery only, not as a control-release guarantee.

tool_metadata_findings.documented_effect: Reset JavaScript kernel and clear bindings

tool_metadata_findings.documented_scope: Native computer APIs disabled; browser control entrypoints available

tool_metadata_findings.inspection: Available nested tool names matching computer/cua/sky and release/control-status patterns
tool_metadata_findings.result: No dedicated Windows app-control release or ownership-status tool exposed

official_sources.retrieval: Fetched full official Computer Use page using fetch_openai_doc after official documentation search
official_sources.finding: Windows Computer Use acts on the active desktop and foreground. The page does not specify a callable release operation or release receipt.
User takeover/stop guidance is present; it is not a documented agent-callable release-and-verify API.

searches: Windows Computer Use stop release session API
search_qualification: Search results alone do not prove absence; the conclusion is anchored to the full installed supported API and fetched official page. Unrelated Responses/API Linux integration examples do not establish a Windows plugin lifecycle operation.
actions_not_taken: No GUI acquisition or window listing/state capture
No app launch or native input
No undocumented helper or emergency-stop bypass
required_external_change: Expose and document a supported release operation with a receipt or ownership-status observation suitable for explicit verification.
orchestrator_handoff: Keep GUI-dependent cases blocked by the existing lifecycle gate; continue independent analysis and preparation.
Recheck only after a concrete supported tool/documentation capability change.
Physical Escape stops GUI input and leaves an interrupted action outcome unknown until legitimately reobserved; it does not cancel the overall plan.
Do not claim app control is off based on JS reset, debugger detach, app termination, idle time or this documentation review.
freeze: Final review file; no prior frozen fixture files changed.

measurement.scope: Wall time from tool metadata discovery through official searches, fetched documentation/API review and artifact creation; excludes initial skill/state orientation.
